name: Earth
description: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known astronomical object to harbor life. It has liquid water on its surface, a protective magnetic field, a breathable nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere, and active plate tectonics. Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System.
surface: 71% water, 29% land; mountains, plains, ocean trenches
deepest_point: Mariana Trench — 10,994 m below sea level
highest_point: Mount Everest — 8,849 m above sea level
known_missions_from_earth: All crewed human spaceflights originate from Earth
summary: Earth is our extraordinary home — the only known planet in the universe confirmed to support life. Its unique combination of liquid water, oxygen atmosphere, magnetic protection, and plate tectonics has enabled billions of years of biological evolution. Earth's Moon stabilizes its axial tilt, contributing to a relatively stable climate over geological timescales.
interesting_facts: Earth is the only known planet with confirmed intelligent life
71% of Earth's surface is covered by water — it should really be called 'Ocean'
Earth's inner core is about as hot as the Sun's surface (~5,700°C)
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at 3.8 cm per year
Earth's magnetic field periodically reverses — the last reversal was 780,000 years ago
Earth is the densest planet in the Solar System at 5,513 kg/m³
A day on Earth is actually 23 hours 56 minutes (not 24 hours exactly)
The Amazon rainforest produces about 20% of the world's oxygen
Earth orbits the Sun at 29.78 km/s (107,208 km/h)
Earth's ozone layer protects life from harmful ultraviolet radiation

faq.a: Earth's habitability comes from its liquid water, oxygen-nitrogen atmosphere, magnetic field protecting from solar radiation, moderate temperature range, and its position in the Sun's habitable zone.
Earth is approximately 4.54 billion years old, formed from the solar nebula around the same time as the rest of the Solar System.

faq.q: Does Earth have a magnetic field?
faq.a: Yes. Earth's magnetic field is generated by the movement of molten iron in its outer core. It deflects harmful solar wind particles, making life on the surface possible.

faq.q: How many moons does Earth have?
faq.a: Earth has one natural satellite — the Moon. It's the fifth largest moon in the Solar System, with a diameter of 3,475 km.
No. Earth is an oblate spheroid — slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator due to its rotation. The equatorial diameter is 12,756 km vs polar diameter of 12,714 km.

faq.q: How far is Earth from the Sun?
faq.a: Earth orbits at an average distance of 149.6 million km (1 AU) from the Sun. This distance varies from 147.1 million km (perihelion in January) to 152.1 million km (aphelion in July).

faq.q: What is the deepest point on Earth?
faq.a: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest known point at about 10,994 meters below sea level.

faq.q: How does plate tectonics work on Earth?
faq.a: Earth's crust is divided into tectonic plates that float on the molten mantle. Their movements cause earthquakes, volcanoes, mountain building, and continental drift over millions of years.

faq.q: How many people have left Earth?
faq.a: As of 2024, about 600 people have reached space (100 km altitude). Only 24 humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit (to the Moon), and 12 have walked on the Moon.

faq.q: What is Earth's atmosphere made of?
faq.a: Earth's atmosphere is 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.93% argon, 0.04% carbon dioxide, and trace amounts of other gases. It extends about 10,000 km above the surface.
